question: During the Basic Control Skills test exercises, what does the manual say the examiner scores you on?
choice_a: Pull-ups, back-ups, encroachments, looks, and final position
choice_b: Only how quickly you complete each exercise
choice_c: Only your final parking position
choice_d: Fuel efficiency during the exercise
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for pull-ups, back-ups, encroachments, looks, and final position during the Basic Control Skills exercises.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: According to the manual, what is a "pull-up" during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_b: Backing up on a forward moving exercise
choice_c: Stopping without changing direction
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position, scored on Exercise 2 and Exercise 4.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: What is a "back-up" as defined in the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Backing up on a forward moving exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_b: Pulling forward to clear an encroachment during a backing exercise
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle to check its position while backing
choice_d: Crossing over a boundary line or cone
explanation: The manual states a back-up is backing up on a forward moving exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position, and is scored on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: What is scored as an "encroachment" during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors
choice_b: Pulling forward more than once
choice_c: Sounding the horn before completing the exercise
choice_d: Failing to set the parking brake
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as crossing over or touching exercise boundary lines or cones with any portion of the vehicle other than the mirrors (unless unique vehicle parts are at door mirror height or higher).
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: What is scored as a "look" during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Exiting the vehicle while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's position while backing
choice_b: Checking your mirrors while stopped
choice_c: Sounding the horn upon completion
choice_d: Pulling forward to clear an encroachment
explanation: The manual defines a look as exiting the vehicle while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's external position while backing.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: Before exiting the vehicle to take a "look" during a backing exercise, what must you do?
choice_a: Set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral
choice_b: Turn off the engine completely
choice_c: Sound the horn twice
choice_d: Signal the examiner verbally and wait for a hand raise
explanation: The manual states that when exiting to check the vehicle's position, you must set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral, then safely exit/enter while facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: What may happen if you open your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park) during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_b: It only counts as one free look
choice_c: It is scored as a minor encroachment
choice_d: The examiner will simply ask you to repeat the exercise
explanation: The manual states that opening the door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park) may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-2

question: How many free pull-ups are allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Two
choice_c: Three
choice_d: None
explanation: The manual states you are allowed one free pull-up on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and may exit the vehicle only one time to check around it.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-2

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups and a maximum of two exits to check around the vehicle
choice_b: One free pull-up and one exit
choice_c: Three free pull-ups and unlimited exits
choice_d: No free pull-ups but unlimited exits
explanation: The manual states you are allowed two free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times to check around the vehicle during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-3

question: How many free looks are permitted on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing compared to Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: Two free looks on Exercise 4 versus one free look on Exercise 2
choice_b: One free look on Exercise 4 versus two free looks on Exercise 2
choice_c: The same number of free looks on both exercises
choice_d: No free looks are permitted on either exercise
explanation: The manual states you may be allowed a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and two free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: What happens if you fail to follow the examiner's instructions for completing a Basic Control Skills exercise as directed?
choice_a: It may result in automatic failure and the test may be terminated by the examiner
choice_b: You are given a warning and one retry
choice_c: You lose only points, but the test continues
choice_d: The exercise is repeated from the beginning
explanation: The manual states failure to follow examiner instructions for completing the exercise as directed may result in automatic failure and the test may be terminated by the examiner.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-2

question: In Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, where must the front most part of the vehicle end up?
choice_a: Within the box at the end of the alley without going past it
choice_b: As close as possible to the far cones
choice_c: Within three feet of the end of the alley
choice_d: Anywhere before the stop line
explanation: The manual states you must stop with the front most part of the vehicle within the box at the end of the alley without going past it, stopping only once.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-2

question: In Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, how far must you back until the front of your vehicle has cleared?
choice_a: Until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley
choice_b: Until the rear of the vehicle touches the boundary line
choice_c: Exactly three feet from the starting point
choice_d: Until signaled by a horn from the examiner
explanation: The manual instructs you to back straight through the alley until the front of your vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-2

question: In Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, how many free back-ups are allowed and can you exit the vehicle?
choice_a: There are no free back-ups, and you are not permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise
choice_b: One free back-up and one exit are allowed
choice_c: Two free back-ups are allowed but no exits
choice_d: Unlimited back-ups are allowed but only one exit
explanation: The manual explicitly states there are NO free back-ups on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, and you are NOT permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-2

question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, how close must the rear most part of the vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
choice_a: Within three feet of the rear of the alley
choice_b: Within one foot of the rear of the alley
choice_c: Exactly touching the rear boundary line
choice_d: Within five feet of the rear of the alley
explanation: The manual states you must bring the rear most part of your vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley when offset backing in Exercise 4.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-3

question: What must you do when you have completed a Basic Control Skills backing exercise to inform the examiner?
choice_a: Set your parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound your horn
choice_b: Turn off the engine and wave to the examiner
choice_c: Flash your headlights twice
choice_d: Exit the vehicle and report verbally
explanation: The manual repeatedly states that upon completing an exercise, you must set your parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound your horn to inform the examiner and allow scoring of your final position.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-2

question: According to the manual, what must you pass before you can proceed to the Road Test?
choice_a: The Basic Control Skills test
choice_b: The vehicle inspection test only
choice_c: A written knowledge test on backing
choice_d: There is no prerequisite test
explanation: The manual states that the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before you can proceed to the Road Test.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-3

question: During the on-road driving test, what must you do at all times according to the manual?
choice_a: Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs/signals/laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation
choice_b: Drive at exactly the posted speed limit at all times
choice_c: Keep both hands on the wheel except when signaling
choice_d: Announce every maneuver out loud to the examiner
explanation: The manual states that at all times during the test you must wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-1

question: According to the manual, when does "unsafe coasting" occur while approaching a turn?
choice_a: When your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle
choice_b: Whenever you release the accelerator before a turn
choice_c: When you brake more than once before turning
choice_d: When your speed drops below 10 mph before the turn
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-1

question: When driving through an intersection during the on-road test, what should you NOT do?
choice_a: Change lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_b: Check traffic thoroughly in all directions
choice_c: Yield to pedestrians in the intersection
choice_d: Keep your hands on the wheel
explanation: The manual states that when driving through an intersection, you should not change lanes while proceeding through it.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-1

question: As you approach an intersection and must stop, what should you avoid doing?
choice_a: Coasting; your vehicle must not roll forward or backward
choice_b: Using your mirrors
choice_c: Downshifting before the stop
choice_d: Checking traffic in all directions
explanation: The manual states that if necessary you must come to a complete stop with no coasting, and your vehicle must not roll forward or backward.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-1

question: During the Urban Business portion of the road test, where should your vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: Centered in the proper lane (right-most lane), keeping up with traffic flow but not exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_b: In the left-most lane to allow for turns
choice_c: Straddling two lanes for visibility
choice_d: As close to the curb as possible at all times
explanation: The manual states your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) and you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-2

question: For vehicles required to stop at railroad crossings (buses, school buses, or placarded vehicles), how close must the vehicle stop to the nearest rail?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_b: Within 25 feet but not less than 10 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: Exactly 20 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: Within 100 feet but not less than 50 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual states these vehicles should stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-2

question: According to the Lane Usage general driving behavior category, where should you finish a left turn on a multiple lane road?
choice_a: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_b: In the left-most available lane
choice_c: In the right-most (curb) lane
choice_d: In any lane that is clear of traffic
explanation: The manual states you should complete a turn in the proper lane on a multiple lane road, finishing a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-4
